claims.text: A Pulumi package is the unit of versioning and distribution, and the components inside it inherit the package's version.
Pulumi recommends structuring Git repositories so that each repository contains exactly one package containing a cohesive set of components.
For a source-based plugin package, the package's version is the Git tag on the repository.
A source-based plugin package is distributed as source code in a Git repository.
Publishing a source-based package to the Pulumi IDP Private Registry is a two-step flow: apply a semver Git tag (e.g., v1.2.3) to the repository, then run `pulumi package publish`.
`pulumi package publish` sends the package metadata to Pulumi Cloud and places the package in the Private Registry.
Publishing to the Private Registry is typically performed by a CI/CD pipeline that runs on tag.
Semver-tagged releases are only required for publishing to the Private Registry.
Source-based packages referenced directly from a `Pulumi.yaml` file can use any Git ref (tag, branch, or commit), regardless of whether it is a valid semantic version.

An executable-based plugin package is distributed as a pre-built plugin binary, typically alongside per-language SDKs published to package feeds (npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven, the Go module proxy, or private equivalents).
The version of an executable-based package is the version embedded in the published binary and SDKs.
Pulumi Cloud customers can additionally publish an executable-based package to the Private Registry via `pulumi package publish`.
In both source-based and executable-based cases, the released artifact is a single, semantically-versioned Pulumi package.
A repository containing multiple packages must either release them in lockstep or invent per-package release tooling that fights the way Pulumi naturally consumes packages.
Multiple components inside a single package are supported and their components ship together at the package's version.

Referenced internal link targets exist: /docs/iac/concepts/packages/, /docs/iac/concepts/components/, packaging-components anchors #source-based-plugin-packages and #executable-based-plugin-packages, /docs/idp/concepts/private-registry/, /docs/iac/cli/commands/pulumi_package_publish/.
The Amazon EKS package in the Pulumi Registry bundles a managed Kubernetes cluster component along with supporting components needed to secure and operate it.
The components in the Amazon EKS package are almost always used together and tend to evolve together, so a shared semantic version makes sense.
A single `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repository root defines the package, with components living alongside it.
The example repository layout places `PulumiPlugin.yaml` at the repo root with components in a `components/` directory (EksCluster, EksIam).
Pulumi does not recommend using a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
It is technically possible to use a single monorepo containing one giant package for all of an organization's components.
Bundling unrelated components in one package forfeits meaningful semantic versioning, because every package release versions every component the same way regardless of whether each changed.

In a package with two unrelated components, an enhancement to ComponentA yields v1.1.0 and a later breaking change to ComponentB yields v2.0.0, decoupling the version number from each component's actual evolution.
The importance of the one-package-per-repository principles grows as an organization's adoption of Pulumi grows.
Following these repository structuring practices improves the reliability, maintainability, and delivery speed of the packages an organization builds and consumes.
